detailed_description: The Word Counter tool gives writers, students, editors, marketers, and developers a fast way to measure text length directly in the browser. Paste text into the input box and the page updates the core metrics immediately: words, total characters, characters without spaces, sentences, paragraphs, and lines. This is useful when you need to keep a meta description near a target length, check a social post before publishing, estimate a short article draft, or compare multiple versions of copy without opening a full writing suite. The counter is intentionally simple and transparent: it treats whitespace-separated text as words, punctuation marks as sentence boundaries, blank-line groups as paragraphs, and newline characters as line breaks. Because the result is shown beside the input, you can revise a sentence and see the count change as you type.
usage_steps: Paste or type your text into the main input area.
Review the word, character, character-without-spaces, sentence, paragraph, and line cards below the input.
Edit the text until the counts match your writing, SEO, academic, or product-copy target.
Use the character-without-spaces count when a platform ignores whitespace, and the total character count when spaces matter.
Click Clear when you want to remove the current text and start a new count.
usage_examples: A content marketer checks whether a draft meta description is close to a 155-character target before adding it to a CMS.
A student confirms that an assignment introduction stays within a required word-count range.
A product manager compares two short feature descriptions and keeps the clearer version under a UI character limit.
A documentation writer checks paragraph and line counts while trimming release notes for readability.

faqs.question: Does the Word Counter upload or store my text?
faqs.answer: No. The tool runs in your browser page and updates the counts from the text you enter. Avoid pasting sensitive information into any online page unless your workflow allows it.

faqs.question: How does the tool count words?
faqs.answer: It counts words by trimming the text and splitting it on whitespace. This is a practical count for drafts, SEO copy, notes, and everyday writing checks.

faqs.question: What is the difference between characters and characters without spaces?
faqs.answer: Characters includes every letter, number, symbol, punctuation mark, and space. Characters without spaces removes whitespace first, which is useful for platforms that ignore spaces in limits.

faqs.question: Can I use it for SEO titles and meta descriptions?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paste the title or description and use the character cards as a quick length check before publishing. Search snippets can still vary by query and device, so treat the count as guidance.

faqs.question: Why might the sentence count differ from a grammar checker?
faqs.answer: This page uses punctuation-based sentence counting for speed and clarity. Grammar tools may apply more language-specific rules, so small differences are expected for abbreviations or unusual punctuation.
